title: Anchor-based embedding store with windowed invalidation and compact dedupe manifests
creator: Miguel Santos
description: Replace current prefix-only caching heuristic with an anchor-based embedding store that records compact content fingerprints and supports windowed invalidation policies. Goal: improve cache hit rate for short-to-medium prefixes, reduce duplicate embedding compute across tenants, and bound staleness with low-coordination invalidation primitives.
background: Current embedding cache is optimized for exact prefix matches and large canonicalization paths. We see misses for small user prefixes and near-duplicates that cause repeated compute and higher latency on reranking endpoints. Eviction/invalidation is coarse-grained, which either leads to stale embeddings being served or aggressive eviction that hurts hit rates. We need an approach that captures common sub-token anchors, de-duplicates at ingestion, and lets us invalidate or TTL entries with minimal cross-region coordination.
proposed_solution: Introduce an anchor manifest model: split ingested content (normalized text) into overlapping anchor windows (n-gram shingles plus sentence anchors). For each anchor compute a compact 64-bit content fingerprint (stable salted hash) and store a mapping anchor -> embedding pointer in a tiered store (in-memory hash + SSD manifest). Maintain per-tenant anchor manifests that list anchor fingerprints and generation stamps. Invalidation uses windowed generation numbers and lightweight tombstone leases: when a document changes, we bump its manifest generation; on lookup a miss or stale generation triggers background refresh rather than blocking the request. Deduplication occurs at write-time by checking anchor fingerprints with a Bloom filter + manifest lookup and reusing existing embedding vectors when similarity/threshold is satisfied. Use an LRU on hot anchors with an SSD-backed cold store to bound memory. Minimize cross-region coordination using monotonic generation ids stored in local metadata stores and conflict-free tombstones for eventual convergence.
technical_design_notes: - Normalization: unicode NFC, whitespace collapse, lowercasing for non-proper-nouns, strip punctuation except sentence boundaries. - Anchors: combine fixed-size character shingles (e.g., 64-char overlap windows) and sentence-level anchors. - Fingerprint: xxh3_64 + tenant-specific salting to avoid cross-tenant collisions; store fingerprint hex. - Manifest: per-tenant, append-only compact manifest file with entries [fingerprint,generation,store_pointer,quality_score,source-canonical-id]. Manifests are delta-compressed and snapshot periodically. - Bloom prefilter: 8-bit Bloom for in-memory quick negative; false positives are handled by manifest lookup. - Dedup thresholding: exact fingerprint -> reuse; near-duplicate detection via cosine on a cheap projection (e.g., 256-d int8 sketch) when canonicalization similarity > 0.85 triggers reuse with a freshness penalty metric. - Invalidation: generation bump + lease tombstone with TTL (configurable by project), background rehydrate process fetches fresh embeddings. - Consistency: best-effort eventual; reads serve existing vectors if generation difference <= tolerance, otherwise serve stale vector and enqueue async refresh to avoid latency spikes. - Storage: hot LRU in Redis/rocksdb in memory-optimized mode, cold manifest on SSD (S3-like for hosted). - Metrics: per-anchor hit/miss, reuse_ratio, stale_serves, invalidation_rate, async_rehydrate_latency.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged internal canary: route 5% of reranking traffic in us-west to use anchor-store reads-only for hits. 2) Measure hit rate and latency, validate correctness on synthetic replay of customer logs. 3) Enable write-path dedupe for non-sensitive tenants on canary. 4) Expand to 25%–50% with write-path and async refresh enabled. 5) Full rollout with tenant opt-outs and per-tenant TTL. 6) Post-rollout: enable SSD-backed cold store lifecycle and snapshot compaction weekly.
acceptance_criteria: Anchor-store must increase overall embedding cache hit rate by >= 12% on our reranking workload during canary compared to baseline.
99th percentile latency for reranking lookup path must not increase by more than 5ms in canary traffic.
Deduplication must reduce unique embedding compute by >= 18% for tenants with high near-duplicate traffic patterns.
Manifest generation and tombstone mechanism must converge within configured TTL without manual intervention in cross-AZ failover tests.
All stored fingerprints and manifests must be encrypted at rest and access-controlled by tenant ID via existing KMS integrations.
Documented smoke tests exist in the infra repo and run in CI; synthetic replay shows no semantic regressions on held-out rerank evaluations.
Rollout plan executed behind a feature flag with kill-switch and metrics dashboards available in Console.
No customer-facing error rates related to embedding reads or reranking should exceed existing baseline during rollout (<= baseline + 0.1%).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Fingerprint collisions cause wrong vector reuse. Mitigation: Use salted 64-bit with tenant salt and backstop exact-text check on collision; conservative threshold for reuse.
Risk: Background rehydrates overload model serving. Mitigation: Rate-limit rehydrate queue, prioritize hot tenants, backpressure to model pool and fall back to on-demand compute if needed.
Risk: Increased operational complexity (manifests, leases). Mitigation: Start with read-only canary, automate manifest snapshotting and provide tooling to inspect manifests per-tenant in Console.
Risk: Cross-region inconsistency. Mitigation: Use monotonic generation ids with local progression and eventual reconciliation; allow per-region tolerance to serve slightly stale vectors within SLO.
Risk: Storage blow-up from anchoring many small shards. Mitigation: Compact manifests weekly, purge low-quality anchors by quality_score and use TTL-based cold deletion.
